standard_prerequisites.name: Suspension and the circle
standard_prerequisites.statement: The suspension of a type has two poles and a meridian path for each point of the type, and the circle has a base point and a loop.
standard_prerequisites.use: They are the two sides of the equivalence, and the maps are defined by their recursion principles.

standard_prerequisites.name: Recursion principles for the circle and the suspension
standard_prerequisites.statement: A map out of the circle is given by a point and a loop at it, and a map out of a suspension is given by two points together with a path between them for each point of the suspended type.
standard_prerequisites.use: Both maps of the equivalence are introduced by these principles with explicit values on the generators.

standard_prerequisites.name: Transport in path spaces and pulled back fibrations
standard_prerequisites.statement: The transport of a path between the endpoints inside a family of path types is computed by conjugating with the action of the map on that path.
standard_prerequisites.use: It turns the two loop cases of the round-trip inductions into the explicit path equations the proof then simplifies.

core_obligations: Define the map from the suspension of the two-point type to the circle by recursion on the suspension, sending both poles to the base point and the two meridians to the loop and to the reflexivity path respectively (source line 593).
Define the map back by recursion on the circle, sending the base point to the north pole and acting on the loop by the composite of one meridian with the inverse of the other (source line 594).

Prove the first round trip by induction on the suspension: the two pole cases are immediate, and the meridian case reduces by transport in path spaces to an equation that is checked for both elements of the two-point type by its induction principle (source lines 597-620).

Prove the second round trip by induction on the circle: the base case is immediate and the loop case reduces to an equation whose left-hand side is computed by the functoriality of the action on paths (source lines 622-633).

proof_roadmap.step: Introduce the two maps by the recursion principles of the suspension and of the circle.
First round trip by induction on the suspension, with the meridian case checked on both points of the two-point type.
Second round trip by induction on the circle, the loop case by functoriality of the action on paths.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled lemma at source lines 588-591: the suspension of the two-point type is the circle. The proof (source lines 592-634) is a construction with two inductions and no delegation: it defines the two maps by the recursion principles with explicit values on the generators (both poles to the base point, the two meridians to the loop and to reflexivity, and the inverse map on the loop as the composite of one meridian with the inverse of the other), then proves one round trip by induction on the suspension, where the meridian case is turned by transport in path spaces into an equation that is then checked separately for each element of the two-point type, and finally proves the other round trip by induction on the circle, where the loop case is computed with the functoriality of the action on paths. Defining the two maps so that they are actually inverse and carrying out both inductions is the substance; the statement alone shows none of it.
